answer: In this PoA design, identity admission requires a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each output serving as the next input; a Wesolowski proof then verifies the result succinctly. Since the chain is inherently sequential, an attacker creating violet, fable, or velvet clones cannot compress each clone’s delay by distributing its work across GPUs. Every identity therefore incurs a strict physical time cost, limiting Sybil identities.
